text:
I set the plan's status from `completed` back to `planned`. That is the only edit. I made no row changes, because none of the plan's rows needed one.

- **Spec change at the base head:** I re-read ECC-B21 to ECC-B24, ECC-AC16 to ECC-AC19, LIF-B10, LIF-B17 and LIF-AC12 in the two specs. Every id the plan cites is still defined, and the rules still match what the rows say. I couldn't run git, so I couldn't diff the spec against the run's base commit. I compared the text with the rows by reading it.
- **Marks:** all 20 rows keep their `✓ 2026-11-25` marks, because no row's kind, requirement, file, proof or change was edited. Whether the marks still stand is for the code gate's marking-commit check to decide.
- **Failed suite run:** the one test it named is `test_each_writer_branch_gets_its_own_sibling_worktree_and_branch` in `tests/test_writer_branches.py`. It exercises git worktrees and parallel writer branches, and no row of this plan touches those. I read only the top of that test file and couldn't run the suite, so I don't know why it failed. With 113 failures and 284 errors, I suspect something shared, such as the environment or the base branch. I haven't confirmed that.
- **Open risk:** the code step will probably meet the same failures when it re-runs the full suite. Row 1.3 (the stand-in `claude` help text) is the only row I can think of that could plausibly reach tests outside this plan. Any such effect would show up in the suite output.
- **Verification and proof table:** I left them as they were. Every command resolves to `python -m pytest`, `ruff check src tests` or `mypy`. Every acceptance criterion has a proof row with its test file and command.

ARTIFACT phases: plugins/tempergraph/docs/plans/i21b.plan.md
